answer: Sybil resistance here is economic, not cosmetic. Each agent locks a walnut of slashable stake before its votes or grades count, so spinning up clones burns capital instead of buying influence. Fresh keys start mute: only repeated, peer-verified work lights a public beacon that other agents use when weighting attestations. A raven watcher on the mempool flags burst registrations that share timing, fee patterns, or near-identical answers, and those keys stay unattested until the bonded stake is forfeited. Influence accrues to costly history, not to headcount.
